title: Self-service sign-up (route 4): sign-up, first credential mail, forced password change, first sign-in, one stock call, cleanup
description: T-3152, route 4 of the tenant-creation routes (PM 27 Nov, item 11). Route 3 needs an existing realm; the sign-up creates it and mails the first credential (signup/provisioning.ex send_credential -> Messages.first_credential). Expectations come from the code: the sign-up form takes no password (config password_required=false; the interim is a mailed temporary password), POST /api/signup answers 202 check_your_mail and nothing else, the tenant is made only after POST /api/signup/verify with the token of the verification mail, and the first-credential mail (subject 'Your workspace account') carries the temporary password and the forced change at first sign-in. The runner address is uat-tmp-<run_id>@uat.letflow.internal (mail trap); synthetic names only; no qoimeks tenant is touched. S1-S5 and S11 run today (S1 is RED when the sign-up is switched off, as on QA on 2026-11-26: 'sign-up not enabled'). S6-S10 are blocked_by the one step the runner cannot do (take the token of the verification mail and open the link; owner: operator, a runner task); each reports NOT RUN, never a pass. The cleanup deactivates and then purges only the tenant uat-tmp-<run_id> (200, or 404 when nothing was made); the platform residue check fails the run on a leftover active uat-tmp-* tenant. The file is NOT in test/uat/pilot-scenarios.txt until it is green on QA.

inputs.verify_token: <taken from the verification mail by the runner step that does not exist yet>

steps.says: Anyone may read the public sign-up config: it is switched on and offers the three languages. If it answers 404 the sign-up is not enabled on this build: RED, reason 'sign-up not enabled'.
A request that does not accept the terms is refused 422 and names the field.
A good request is answered 202 check_your_mail, whether or not the address is known.
The verification mail reaches the throwaway address in the mail trap, with no human step. Only recipient, subject and message id are read.

steps.blocked_by: owner: operator (runner task): no runner step takes the token out of the verification mail and POSTs /api/signup/verify (wait_mail never reads a body; the SPA page does it for a person). Until it exists the tenant is never created and every step after the mail is NOT RUN, never a pass
steps.says: Open the verification link: POST /api/signup/verify with the token of the mail (routers/signup.ex 'verify': 200 verified, 400 invalid_or_expired_link, 409 slug_taken). Verifying starts the tenant creation (Provisioning.start_async) with the slug as host label.

steps.says: With no human step the new tenant becomes active (the provisioner makes the realm and the tenant after the verification; the read repeats until it holds). D-195: if it waits for a person it is RED. The realm is read from the registry, never derived from the slug.

steps.says: The first administrator signs in with the temporary password of the first-credential mail (subject 'Your workspace account'; only the runner reads the body, in memory, never in the log), does the forced password change at the identity provider with a password made in memory, and takes the token of the new realm.

steps.says: The tenant opens for its new administrator: the access list answers 200 with the role TENANT_ADMIN.

steps.blocked_by: owner: operator (runner task): no runner step takes the token out of the verification mail and POSTs /api/signup/verify (wait_mail never reads a body; the SPA page does it for a person). steps.says: ONE stock call as that admin: the stock document list answers 200, which proves the new tenant is runnable. A 404 means the sign-up path installs no stock module: a finding of the first red run.
A reserved word as the slug is refused 422 (slug_taken is only answered at verification; a repeated sign-up is accepted neutrally).

cleanup.says: Deactivate only the throwaway tenant this run may have made (slug uat-tmp-<run_id>, never a permanent one). Runs after a failed sign-up too: 404 means nothing was made.
Purge the throwaway tenant after its deactivation (200), or nothing to purge (404).
